title: 荒城の月 (Kōjō no Tsuki — Moon Over the Ruined Castle)
description: One of Japan's most famous art songs. Lyrics by 土井晩翠 (Doi Bansui, 1898), music by 滝廉太郎 (Taki Rentarō, 1901). Four verses in classical Japanese (文語体) meditate on the contrast between a castle's glorious past — cherry blossom banquets in spring, moonlit campaigns in autumn — and its present ruin, where only ivy and wind remain. Key literary vocabulary: 高楼 (tower), 巡る盃 (circling cups of sake), 栄枯 (rise and fall of fortune). Required learning in Japanese schools.
